title: Forward Deployed Computational Biologist
description: About us Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed. Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity. K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners. Please submit your CV in English Salary range: $128,000 - $150,000 Ideal start date: January or February 2027 About the role: We are seeking a Forward Deployed Computational Biologist to operate at the intersection of AI, software systems, and biology. In this role, you will work directly with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to design, build, and deploy production-grade AI solutions for complex scientific problems as part of Owkin’s agentic platform, K Pro, to fully meet specific customer needs. This is a hands-on, client-facing role. You will spend time at the customer’s premises, turning ambiguous scientific challenges—such as discovering novel drug targets or disease subtypes—into reliable and scalable agentic solutions. You will be responsible for both the scientific rigor of the analytical workflows and the technical robustness of their implementation and deployment, bridging the gap between science and real-world application. In particular, you will: Deploy & Custom-build : Tailor Owkin’s agentic AI platform, K Pro, to specific client needs by implementing new analytical workflows, and integrate our platform into the clients’ existing workflows. Solve Scientific Problems : Translate complex biological and operational questions into concrete computational workflows, utilizing deep clinical and multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, etc.) and computational biology methodologies. Rapid Prototyping : Iterate quickly with users to validate solutions, balancing speed and quality to ensure effective, measurable impact. Collaboration : Work alongside Customer Success Managers, R&D data scientists, biologists, and software engineers to ensure the delivery of high-quality scientific insights. Knowledge Transfer : Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders—from clinicians and biologists to technical engineering teams—to ensure alignment and adoption. Participation in a team-wide on-call rotation is required. This role requires frequent international travel to support our global operations and client needs. Anticipated destinations include the Owkin Paris office as well as various client premises across the UK, US, France, Germany, and Switzerland. To facilitate this travel schedule, the successful candidate must be based in close proximity to a major international airport or major train station . About you Required qualifications / experience: Education : MSc/PhD in Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Biology, Computer Science, or a related field. Proven expertise and impact in analyzing complex data, such as real-world clinical data and multimodal omics (e.g, bulk, spatial/single-cell, proteomics) and high-throughput experimental data. Biological knowledge : Strong knowledge of molecular biology and at least one major therapeutic area (oncology, Immunology & Inflammation, neurology, …). Bias for action : Ability to operate in fast-paced environments, managing ambiguity, and driving progress toward delivery. Engineering Proficiency : Very strong programming skills in Python; ability to both ideate and conduct exploratory analyses and data visualisations to aid interpretation; and write clean, production-grade code. Strong familiarity with coding agents. AI/ML Experience : Familiarity with machine learning concepts (e.g., cross-validation, statistical tests) and frameworks (scikit-learn, XGBoost, etc.). Experience with LLMs and agentic AI frameworks is a plus. Communication : Exceptional ability to translate scientific complexity for non-technical internal and external stakeholders. Preferred qualifications/bonus: Experience in a Biotech/Pharma environment and excellent understanding of the different steps and respective needs of the typical Pharma drug discovery pipeline. Demonstrated ability to write production-level code in deployed products. #LI-MD1 What we offer Flexible work organization Friendly and informal working environment Opportunity to work with an international team with high technical and scientific backgrounds Recruitment Process & Security Please complete the form and submit your CV. title: Research Associate II, Pluvinage Lab
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

We are seeking a Research Associate to join the Pluvinage Lab at the Arc Institute. Our goal is to improve the lives of patients with neurological diseases. We do this by exploring undiagnosed autoimmunity in rare mystery cases and common neurodegenerative conditions alike. Starting with clinical observations and primary patient tissue, we use functional genomics, protein display technologies, and computational tools to embark on deep mechanistic dives into the contribution of autoimmunity to cognitive function. Your work will have the potential to uncover novel autoantibodies that drive cognitive decline in autoimmune encephalitis, that modulate cognitive decline in dementia, and that promote cognitive resilience in healthy brain aging.

The questions we ask:

  1. How do autoantibodies regulate cognition?
  2. What is the source, target, and mechanism of pathogenic autoantibodies in neurological disease?
  3. How can we eliminate pathogenic autoantibodies while leaving the rest of the immune system intact?
  4. How does comorbid autoimmunity contribute to cognitive decline in neurodegeneration?
  5. Are there protective autoantibodies that promote cognitive resilience in healthy brain aging?

The approaches we take: discovery-driven projects starting with human samples (cerebrospinal fluid, PBMCs, brain tissue) from curated cohorts of patients with neurological diseases, CRISPR screens, phage display, immune repertoire sequencing.

In this role, you will work closely with senior lab members to drive high-throughput antibody discovery in autoimmune neurology and neurodegeneration. You will contribute across the full experimental workflow: designing constructs and libraries, cloning and validating reagents, executing screens across several protein display technologies, and analyzing and validating discoveries. This is a hands-on position for someone who enjoys both the precision of molecular biology and the challenge of making complex discovery workflows reproducible and scalable. Your work will help advance new diagnostic approaches from bench to bedside.

About you

  • You are detail-oriented and rigorous, taking pride in well-designed experiments, reliable reagents, and reproducible results.
  • You are curious and self-motivated, with a strong foundation in molecular biology and an eagerness to learn new protein display and antibody discovery technologies.
  • You enjoy working across an entire experimental workflow, from sequence design and cloning to screening and data analysis.
  • You are organized and able to manage multiple experiments while maintaining careful sample tracking and documentation.
  • You collaborate closely with others, communicate results and challenges openly, and troubleshoot thoughtfully.
  • You are passionate about translating discoveries into better diagnostics for patients with neurological disease.
  • This position is designed as a training role for individuals preparing to apply to a PhD program. The work associated with this role is expected to last approximately two years, giving you time to build a portfolio of research to support future applications.

In this position you will

  • Build Discovery Reagents: Work with senior lab members to design DNA constructs and protein display libraries; perform molecular cloning, sequence verification, and quality control of constructs and libraries.
  • Execute High-Throughput Screens: Prepare reagents and patient samples, carry out antibody discovery and antigen-identification workflows across multiple protein display platforms, and maintain rigorous controls and sample tracking throughout.
  • Analyze and Validate Discoveries: Process screening data using established analysis workflows, assess data quality and reproducibility, and work with senior lab members to prioritize hits and validate antibody–antigen interactions using complementary assays.
  • Develop and Optimize Workflows: Work with senior lab members to troubleshoot experiments, compare assay conditions, and help improve the sensitivity, specificity, throughput, and reproducibility of discovery methods.
  • Maintain Research Quality: Keep complete experimental records, document protocols and analysis steps, and maintain organized inventories of samples, constructs, libraries, and reagents.
  • Contribute to a Collaborative Lab: Communicate progress at lab meetings, coordinate experiments with senior lab members and collaborators, and contribute to shared lab operations, equipment maintenance, and protocol training.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, immunology, genetics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant laboratory experience.
  • 2+ years of relevant experience in an academic or industry setting (including independent lab work during your undergraduate studies).
  • Hands-on research experience in molecular biology
  • Demonstrated ability to execute multistep experimental protocols accurately, use appropriate controls, and maintain clear and complete laboratory records.
  • Growth mindset to stretch your scientific skillset in a supportive environment, and the awareness to know when to ask for help.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, including careful tracking of samples, reagents, and experimental conditions.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work both independently on established workflows and collaboratively with senior scientists.
  • Commitment to rigorous, reproducible research and a strong interest in antibody discovery and its diagnostic applications.

The base salary for this position is $75,900. This amount does not include benefits or other forms of compensation.

title: Manager of Bioinformatics (Oncology Product Development)
description:
Natera is currently seeking a Bioinformatics Manager to join the Bioinformatics team focused on Oncology Product Development. In this role, the individual will manage a team of Bioinformaticians and Data Scientists and provide technical leadership in the design, development and validation of ctDNA-based diagnostic tests. This position requires extensive cross-functional collaboration with biostatistics, molecular biology, software engineering and commercial departments. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in bioinformatics and data science, optimally with experience in the LDT assay development space, and an established record of project and technical leadership.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide technical leadership for product development projects by representing the bioinformatics team in cross-functional interactions and moving products through the full development process through validation and commercial launch.
  • Lead the effort to optimize workflows, improve tools and pressure test analysis pipelines for diagnostic tests, including the detection of cancer-associated variants and the implementation of evidence-based quality control thresholds.
  • Supervise bioinformatics scientists and data scientists, managing their technical contributions, prioritizing resources, and taking responsibility for their technical and professional development.
  • Provide input on experiment design, analysis and interpretation based on expert understanding of Natera’s technology and relevant mathematical principles.
  • Work at a high level of independence and responsibilities in carrying out assignments.
  • Contribute to our intellectual property portfolio.
  • Set standards for rigorous data analysis and lead the production of high-quality documentation. 

QUALIFICATIONS:

Requirements:

  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in a quantitative discipline (bioinformatics, engineering, applied mathematics, statistics, or similar).
  • Minimum of 4-8 years of post-graduate experience in a data science and/or bioinformatics role and 1-3 years of experience as technical lead in diagnostics or a related field
  • Experience moving algorithm-based products through commercialization and launch in a medical or biological application such as diagnostic testing, medical imaging, or biotechnology
  • 1-2 years of management experience leading a technical team with demonstrable evidence of leadership and team management skills.

Desirable, but not required:

  • Prior experience analyzing cancer-associated variant detection data

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

  • Experience using Python or R for scientific data analysis and visualization.
  • Strong foundation in statistical modeling/machine learning, including probability theory and estimation/classification methods.
  • Experience with analysis of next-generation sequencing data, preferably including algorithm development or optimization.
  • Proven ability to apply mathematical principles to solve real estimation problems and implement practical solutions.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills to independently make sound judgments and find creative solutions to moderately complex problems.
  • Experience leading technical projects, including defining and meeting project milestones, delegating tasks to more junior team members, and ensuring the quality of technical deliverables.
  • Excellent communication skills and the desire to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment.

Compensation & Total Rewards 

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of  hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:

  • Annual performance incentive bonus

  • Long-term equity awards

  • Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Generous paid time off and company holidays

  • Additional wellness and work-life benefits

Compensation Range
$154,000—$192,500 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

For more information, visit www.natera.com.

Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws.

Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. title: Associate Scientist III, Cardiac Modeling
description: The Opportunity insitro is a physical AI company dedicated to unlocking causal human biology and accelerating the delivery of better medicines to patients. Our unique Virtual Human™ platform identifies novel, high-impact genetic intervention points, which our TherML™ platform translates into therapeutics—whether small molecules, biologics, or oligos. With multiple programs in metabolic disease and neuroscience advancing toward the clinic, and our first IND submission slated for the second half of this year, we are at a pivotal inflection point. We are seeking an Associate Scientist III to join our cardiac disease biology team. In this role, you will support the development and application of iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte (iPSC-CM) models to study the genetic and molecular underpinnings of cardiovascular disease — working at the intersection of human stem cell biology, cardiac physiology, and scalable experimental platforms to generate the datasets that fuel our ML-driven drug discovery efforts. You will design and execute experiments, optimize differentiation workflows, develop functional and scalable functional assays to connect cellular phenotypes to disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets. Based in South San Francisco, this position reports directly to Senior Scientist, Cardiometabolic Disease - Translational Genetics and requires you to be onsite at our South San Francisco office 5 days per week . Responsibilities iPSC-CM Platform & Model Development Differentiation & QC: Support the generation and maintenance of iPSC lines and their differentiation into cardiomyocytes in 2D format (monolayers), implementing rigorous quality control points at each stage of the pipeline and with emphasis on production scalability Genetic Disease Models: Assist in building isogenic iPSC-CM disease models — including patient and CRISPR-edited lines carrying disease-associated variants — and characterizing the cellular model to study cardiovascular pathophysiology Functional Assays & Disease Modeling Functional Readouts: Support the development and optimization of functional assays relevant to cardiovascular disease —contractility, electrophysiology, calcium handling, stress responses, high-content imaging — in formats compatible with high-throughput data acquisition Rigor & Reproducibility: Documentation including writing/reviewing technical procedures and SOPs, presentation of results in team meetings and maintaining laboratory notebook with scientific rigor Cross-functional Partnership Target Identification: Contribute to target identification and validation efforts by connecting cellular phenotypes to human genetic evidence, aligning around the team and company goals to advance drug discovery About You Experience & Qualifications Qualifications and previous experience: A bachelor’s or master’s degree in biology, biochemistry, or related discipline with at least 2 years of relevant experience in the biotech/biopharma industry Cell culture and iPSC-CM Expertise: Deep hands-on experience in iPSC culture, cardiac directed differentiation and iPSC-CM model characterization in 2D (monolayer) format. title: Technical Sales Manager - Growth Accounts (US Overlay)
description:
WHO ARE WE

Parse Biosciences, a QIAGEN company, is a global life sciences company whose mission is to accelerate progress in human health and scientific research. Empowering researchers to perform single cell sequencing with unprecedented scale and ease, its pioneering approach has enabled groundbreaking discoveries in cancer treatment, tissue repair, stem cell therapy, kidney and liver disease, brain development, and the immune system.

With technology developed at The University of Washington, Parse has raised over $100 million in capital and is now used by over 3.000 customers across the world. Our growing portfolio of products includes Evercode Whole Transcriptome, Evercode TCR, BCR, Gene Capture, and Trailmaker, our data analysis solution.

Parse Biosciences is based in Seattle, Washington's vibrant South Lake Union district, where we recently opened a 34,000 square foot headquarters and state-of-the-art laboratory.

THE POSITION

As a Technical Sales (Account) Manager, you will be responsible for achieving sales objectives for our single cell RNA sequencing products through the development of new business and management of current customer accounts. You will be expected to create and execute a sales strategy across academic, biotech, and pharmaceutical accounts while working closely with Field Application Scientists and other Parse team members. Candidates should have strong technical skills, sales skills, the ability to develop and manage customer relationships, and a drive to overachieve. Gaining a deep understanding of the single cell market and Parse’s products will be critical to success.  You will accelerate growth in both named Key Accounts and select territories across the United States.  You will act as a specialist to move an emerging segment faster than one rep can on their own.

TERRITORY AND TRAVEL

Key accounts will be defined and open territory focus will change based on business needs.  The position will require travel approximately 50% of the time. 

IN THIS POSITION, YOU WILL

• Generate and manage both high volume and large complex sales.
• Ensure customers are satisfied and making rapid experimental progress.
• Develop, maintain, and grow repeat business while maintaining strong relationships.
• Prospect effectively to generate an immediate, medium, and long-term sales pipelines to ensure consistent quota obtainment.
• Negotiate and close deals while minimizing discounting.
• Effectively communicate technical advantages to customers.
• Develop a quarterly and yearly business plan that incorporates both strategic and tactical activities.
• Prioritize and qualify inbound leads.
• Provide management with insight on competition, market trends, and customer feedback.

Khan Academy is a nonprofit with the mission to deliver a free, world-class education to anyone, anywhere. ABOUT KHAN ACADEMY KIDS

Khan Academy Kids is a free and fun learning program for children ages 2 to 8. Kodi Bear and a cast of animated characters lead children on a personalized education journey filled with fun, standards-aligned activities in early literacy, math, executive functioning and social emotional skills. Built by a small but mighty team, Khan Academy Kids is used by millions of children in homes and classrooms around the world.

Our students, teachers, and parents come from all walks of life, and so do we. Our team includes people from academia, traditional/non-traditional education, big tech companies, and tiny startups. We hire great people from diverse backgrounds and experiences because it makes our company stronger. We value diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging as necessary to achieve our mission and impact the communities we serve. We know that transforming education starts in-house with learning about ourselves and our colleagues. We strive to be world-class in investing in our people and commit to developing you as a professional.

THE ROLE

Khan Academy Kids is looking for an early childhood educator and learning-content developer to build and strengthen learning activities and assessments for children in PreK through 2nd grade.

Working on a small, interdisciplinary team alongside product managers, engineers, designers, and academic experts, the Content Creator will identify gaps in our content library, create and revise learning experiences in English and Spanish, and improve the systems that support content development. Content spans bilingual (English and Spanish) learning activities and direct assessments across early literacy, language, math, and executive function.

We are looking for someone who understands how young children learn, is energized by using data to make content better, and cares deeply about making early learning both rigorous and fun.

OUR COMPANY VALUES

Live & breathe learners

We deeply understand and empathize with our users. We leverage user insights, research, and experience to build content, products, services, and experiences that our users trust and love. Our success is defined by the success of our learners and educators.

We are committed to making learning a joyful process. This informs what we build for our users and the culture we co-create with our teammates, partners and donors.

description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

title: Scientist, Neurodegeneration
description:
Our Mission

Our mission is to restore cell health and resilience through cell rejuvenation to reverse disease, injury, and the disabilities that can occur throughout life.

For more information, see our website at altoslabs.com.

Our Value

Our Single Altos Value: Everyone Owns Achieving Our Inspiring Mission.

Diversity at Altos

Altos Labs has been named one of the Top 3 Biotech Companies and ranked for the second year on the Forbes 2026 Best Startups in America list.  At Altos, exceptional scientists and industry leaders from around the world work together to advance a shared mission. Our intentional focus is on Belonging, so that all employees know that they are valued for their unique perspectives. We are all accountable for sustaining a diverse and inclusive environment.

What You Will Contribute To Altos

 

Join Altos Labs at the Bay Area Discovery Science center and play a pivotal role in our mission to reverse brain aging. We are seeking a driven neuroscientist with deep expertise in neurodegeneration to join our highly collaborative, fast-paced team. In this role, you will work closely with cross-functional experts to discover and validate optimal therapeutic targets for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. If you are passionate about translating complex biology into transformative therapies, we want you on our team.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the Science: Act as the scientific lead for a key segment of our neurodegeneration portfolio. You will shape critical research questions, design robust experiments, and drive studies through to actionable, interpretable conclusions.
  • Model Disease Biology: Design and execute in vivo studies using rodent models of neurodegeneration, strategically selecting models, timepoints, and endpoints tailored to specific biological questions and program stages.
  • Analyze Complex Tissue: Process and analyze both rodent and human brain tissue. This includes dissection, regional sampling, fixation, cryopreservation, sectioning, and comprehensive downstream characterization (molecular, biochemical, and histological).
  • Innovate Quantitative Readouts: Develop and apply precise quantitative readouts for pathology and disease biology, tracking markers such as protein aggregation, neuroinflammation, cell loss, and vascular integrity.
  • Collaborate Across Disciplines: Partner closely with internal experts—including in vivo pharmacology, histology, molecular biology, computational, and program management teams—as well as external collaborators and CROs to seamlessly deliver on shared timelines.
  • Champion Scientific Rigor: Establish and promote the highest technical and cultural standards across our scientific functions. You will help embed foundational practices—such as experimental rigor, blinding, randomization, data provenance, and reproducibility—into our day-to-day operations.
  • Drive Strategic Decisions: Actively contribute to program strategy and high-level decision-making, providing critical input on go/no-go recommendations. We value transparent communication, so you will be expected to flag risks early and candidly.
  • Ensure Data Integrity: Maintain rigorous, traceable records and structured data capture, ensuring your findings can be easily reviewed, reproduced, and built upon by the wider team.
  • Stay Ahead of the Curve: Keep a close pulse on the latest neurodegeneration literature and proactively bring relevant external developments to bear on our internal research programs.

Who You Are 

The level of the position will depend on the qualifications of the selected candidate.

Minimum Qualifications, Knowledge, Skill and Abilities

Core Expertise & Credentials

  • Neurodegeneration Specialist: You hold a Ph.D. in Neuroscience (or a related field) backed by 1+ years of post-doctoral or industry research experience focused on neurodegeneration.
  • Disease Biology Deep-Dive: You bring a robust understanding of neurodegenerative disease biology, including a nuanced perspective on the strengths and limitations of the rodent models used to study it.
  • Proven Track Record: You have an established publication record in the field and are accustomed to presenting your findings at conferences or similar scientific venues.

Technical & Experimental Capabilities

  • Hands-on Analyst: You have extensive, practical experience processing and analyzing both rodent and human brain tissue samples.
  • In Vivo & Imaging: You have practical experience with animal surgeries, behavior, and vascular biology, and are proficient in imaging and behavioral analysis techniques.
  • Therapeutic Fluency: You have experience working with therapeutic modalities relevant to the Central Nervous System (CNS), such as AAV-based approaches, ASOs, or small molecules.
  • Data-Driven Design: You possess strong quantitative and statistical judgment, enabling you to design appropriately powered studies, analyze complex data, and interpret results objectively without over-extrapolating.
  • In Vivo & Imaging: You have practical experience with animal surgeries, behavior, and vascular biology, and are proficient in imaging and behavioral analysis techniques.

Scientific Mindset & Adaptability

  • Fiercely Independent & Rigorous: You are highly self-directed—capable of defining a problem, selecting the right approach, and driving it to a conclusion with minimal oversight. You practice rigorous critical thinking and are always willing to interrogate your own data or change your position when the evidence warrants it.
  • Thrive in Dynamic Environments: You are comfortable and composed in a fast-moving, high-stakes environment where priorities can shift, decisions carry real weight, and quality must be sustained under pressure.

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Cross-Functional Collaborator: You excel at working across disciplines and possess the strong communication skills needed to present complex technical datasets clearly to broad, mixed audiences.
  • Standard Bearer: You are enthusiastic about defining, implementing, and championing technical and cultural standards (like experimental rigor and reproducibility) across our scientific functions.

Preferred Qualifications, Knowledge, Skill and Abilities

  • In Vivo & Imaging: You have practical experience with animal surgeries, behavior, and vascular biology, and are proficient in imaging and behavioral analysis techniques.
  • Omics Interest: You have some exposure to analyzing biological datasets and a strong desire to build deep expertise in transcriptomics, proteomics, or spatial approaches.
  • Technical Foundations: You possess basic skills in bioinformatics data processing or programming (e.g., Python or R) and are eager to apply these to large-scale data management.
  • Human Cohort Awareness: You are interested in expanding your knowledge of working with human post-mortem or biopsy samples and the unique challenges of cohort-level data.
  • Technique Expansion: You are motivated to learn advanced imaging techniques, spatial biology, or high-content quantitative histology to enhance your research.
  • Collaborative Teamwork: You demonstrate strong potential for growth and a commitment to working effectively within a high-performing, collaborative team environment.
  • Clear Communicator: You are a clear and effective communicator, capable of presenting technical information to your peers and cross-functional partners.

This is a hands-on bench role with targeting compositional and reaction design ownership. You will work closely with the Delivery Sciences and biology teams to design and build relevant targeting lipids portfolio for New Limit’s pipeline programs.

What you’ll do

  • Design and develop LNP compositions and conjugation chemistries for antibodies, nanobodies, scFv’s, peptides, and other targeting moieties across multiple structural families, pushing the platform beyond current-generation materials for extra-hepatic targeting.
  • Plan conjugation reactions and purification for these modalities with scale and final purity in mind from the outset, delivering against agreed project timelines.
  • Test targeting lipids for the tLNP platform using an SAR-based approach to guide the next design cycle.
  • Develop conjugation chemistries in-house or work with external partners to get the targeted LNPs for a particular target cell and build processes to support research teams to test the tLNPs in vivo.
  • Turn in vitro and in vivo data from discovery teams into concrete structural hypotheses and optimize the tLNP compositions or the type of targeting molecules used.
  • Present experimental results, and SAR conclusions, authoring protocols and technical reports.

Requirements

  • Analytical characterization across LC-CAD, LC-UV, DLS, CE, bio-layer interferometry and surface plasmon resonance with the ability to deconvolute the data to produce well-characterized tLNPs.

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with novel conjugation chemistries and reaction methods.

  • Exposure to scale-up process development, CMC, or tech transfer to a CDMO.

title: Customer Facing Research Analyst
description:
Customer Facing Research Analyst

Truveta transforms healthcare into intelligence. Built with and owned by US health systems united by a mission of Saving Lives with Data, Truveta powers breakthrough discoveries, auditable data fit for regulatory submissions, and AI that improves patient care.

At Truveta, we are building something that has never existed before, bringing together healthcare, science, and technology to tackle some of the most important challenges in human health. Our mission calls us to think big, move with urgency, and build with purpose. We are looking for exceptional people who are energized by hard problems, inspired by the opportunity to improve health, and committed to building a company and culture where talented people can do their best work.

Our team is a special combination of software, health, and big data experience. We are building a talented team of passionate, mission-oriented, and innovative thinkers. 

Truveta was born in the Pacific Northwest, but we have employees who live across the country.  Our team enjoys the flexibility of a hybrid model and working from anywhere.  In person attendance is required at least once per year for an onsite meeting. 

For overall team productivity, we optimize meeting hours in the pacific time zone. We avoid scheduling recurring meetings that start after 3pm PT, however, ad hoc meetings occur between 8am-6pm Pacific time. #LI-remote

Who We Need 

Truveta is rapidly building a talented and diverse team to tackle complex health and technical challenges. Beyond core capabilities, we are seeking problem solvers, passionate and collaborative teammates, and those willing to roll up their sleeves while making a difference. If you are interested in the opportunity to pursue purposeful work, join a mission-driven team, and build a rewarding career while having fun, Truveta may be the perfect fit for you. 

This Opportunity 

This Customer Facing Research Analyst position is a high impact, customer-facing role that requires a diverse set of skills spanning technical execution, applied research methodology, and relationship management. You will work directly with life sciences partners to translate research questions into analytical approaches, execute studies using real-world Electronic Health Record (EHR) data (~120M+ patients), and guide customers in best practices for real-world evidence generation.

You will play a key role in advancing customer research by helping shape analytical approaches, ensuring methodological rigor, and driving projects forward from question to insight. While customers may define or co-develop study protocols, you will provide guidance on study design, bias considerations, statistical approaches, and interpretation of results. This role requires balancing rapid-response analytical support with deeper, more complex investigations, while maintaining a high bar for scientific rigor and customer experience.

Responsibilities

  • Partner closely with life sciences customers to understand research questions and translate them into analytical approaches
  • Required to excel in providing technical analytics support as well as directly working with customers on calls to troubleshooting customer analysis.
  • Use technical skills to scope out customer analyses requests, produce studies and results using SQL, R and Python within an agreed upon deadline.
  • Build strong, trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, acting as a key partner in advancing their research goals
  • Apply appropriate research methodologies, including cohort design, bias mitigation, and statistical analysis
  • Communicate on the status of various projects and collaborate with success managers to ensure that Truveta clients can be successful with the platform.
  • Guide customers on best practices in real-world data research, including study design tradeoffs and interpretation of results
  • Lead customer-facing discussions to unblock research challenges and drive projects forward
  • Collaborate with customers to support peer-reviewed publications and high-quality research outputs
  • Deliver both rapid-response analyses and deeper, in-depth investigations depending on customer needs
  • Provide technical support and troubleshooting for customer analyses, code, and notebooks
  • Create enablement materials as the Truveta platform evolves to help onboard new researchers to our increasing capabilities.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to investigate data quality and demonstrate data reliability
  • Deliver feedback to internal teams based on customer requests to inform Truveta’s product roadmap.

Required Skills

  • Undergraduate or graduate degree in clinical research, epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, clinical informatics, or a related field
  • 5+ years of experience working in a technical customer-facing role, delivering high-quality research studies & analyses.
  • 3+ years of experience wrangling and analyzing Electronic Health Record data or other Real World Data sources in life science companies, CROs, other EHR data companies or healthcare organizations.
  • Strong proficiency in SQL, R and/or Python for statistical analysis
  • Experience working across large, multi-domain healthcare datasets with millions of patients and hundreds of millions of records, leveraging distributed computing frameworks for scalable analysis.
  • Willingness to learn new coding languages including internal proprietary coding language to analyze data and build cohorts.
  • Strong understanding of real-world evidence principles, including bias, confounding, and study design considerations.
  • Demonstrated experience applying research methodologies, including cohort design and statistical approaches.
  • Experience delivering high-quality product demonstrations that enable customers or stakeholders to understand and effectively leverage data, platform capabilities, and analytical workflows.
  • Proven ability to learn, adapt, and independently drive multiple projects forward in a fast-paced, start-up environment.
  • Strong executive presence with the ability to build credibility and trust across stakeholders and effectively communicate complex technical concepts to both executive and technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

These qualifications are preferred but not required. Candidates will have opportunities to develop these skills over time.

  • Advanced degree (MS, MPH, PhD) in epidemiology, biostatistics, health economics, or related field
  • Experience supporting or contributing to peer-reviewed publications or conference abstracts
  • Knowledge of advanced statistical methods such as regression, propensity score methods, survival analysis, and longitudinal data analysis
  • Experience applying methods for causal inference or handling incomplete data in observational research
  • Experience with Spark/PySpark or distributed data processing
  • Experience with Regression, Propensity Score Matching, Kaplan-Meier Analyses, or Survival Analyses
  • Experience working in customer-facing or consulting-style roles
  • Demonstrated ability to present research findings to both technical and non-technical audiences

Why Truveta?   

Be a part of building something special. Now is the perfect time to join Truveta. We have strong, established leadership with decades of success. We are well-funded. We are building a culture that prioritizes people and their passions across personal, professional and everything in between. Join us as we build an amazing company together.  

We Offer:

  • Interesting and meaningful work for every career stage
  • Great benefits package
  • Comprehensive benefits with strong medical, dental and vision insurance plans
  • 401K plan
  • Professional development & training opportunities for continuous learning
  • Work/life autonomy via flexible work hours and flexible paid time off
  • Generous parental leave
  • Regular team activities (virtual and in-person)
  • The base pay for this position is $110,000 to $160,000. The pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target. Pay is based on several factors including location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  This role is eligible for stock options.

If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents linked here.

title: Product Manager, Care Delivery
description:

Through Maven Enterprise, the company partners with more than 2,300 employers and health plans to provide end-to-end women's and family health programs spanning fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, and menopause and midlife — improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs, and expanding equitable access to high-quality care at scale. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission –  Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including: 

  • TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)
  • Fortune Change the World (2024)
  • CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)
  • Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the Role: 

Care Delivery is the infrastructure that powers how Maven members access care and how our providers deliver it. Every program we run across maternity, fertility, menopause, and pediatrics, depends on it. It's where clinical workflows, provider tooling, and the systems that make care measurable, billable, and scalable at Maven's scale all come together.

We're looking for a Product Manager to help build that platform: the EHR and clinical tooling, provider workflows, messaging, and the data and billing infrastructure that turn Maven's care model into something reliable and scalable. You'll own defined capabilities within the platform and drive them from problem to shipped, in close partnership with engineering, clinical, design, and operations. It's a high-leverage seat. What you build here touches every program Maven offers.

You'll report to the Group Product Manager, Care Delivery, and work closely with our providers, as well as Clinical Product, Member Experience, Operations, and the Data and AI Platform teams.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own specific Care Delivery capabilities end-to-end, provider workflows, clinical documentation, messaging, scheduling and matching, or quality and billing infrastructure, from problem definition through launch and iteration.
  • Make crisp, well-reasoned product decisions, especially where clinical accuracy and provider experience are both at stake.
  • Use AI hands-on to move faster, prototyping with AI tools to test ideas and pressure-test flows before committing engineering time, and identify and build AI-powered capabilities into the care delivery platform where they genuinely improve the provider or member experience.
  • Partner daily with engineering and design to ship reliable platform capabilities, and with clinical and operations partners so that what you build works for real providers and members.
  • Translate regulatory and quality requirements, like HEDIS measures and clinical coding, into clean product experiences that add value without adding friction.
  • Instrument what you ship, watch how it performs, and iterate. Bring data to every decision.
  • Build platform primitives, reusable capabilities that serve many programs, rather than one-off features.
  • Bring a point of view on how AI can improve care delivery workflows, and put it to work in how you build.

What You’ll Bring: 

  • 3+ years in product management, ideally with some time in healthcare tech or another complex, regulated, or operations-heavy domain.
  • A strong executor: you take ambiguous problems, break them down, and ship, without needing everything defined for you.
  • Solid data instincts: you define the right metrics, work with real datasets, and communicate findings clearly to both clinical and commercial audiences.
  • Comfort with technical and clinical complexity: you can hold your own in an engineering sprint and a clinical review, and you're eager to learn the domain fast (FHIR, interoperability, EHR workflows).
  • Genuine care for providers and members: the people using what you build show up in your decisions.
  • Clear, direct communication and strong cross-functional collaboration.
  • Fluency with AI and a genuine desire to build with it: you understand how modern AI models work well enough to know where they're reliable and where they aren't, you reach for AI tools to prototype and think, and you're excited to ship AI-powered features rather than just talk about them.
  • Bonus: experience with EHR or EMR systems, clinical workflows, healthcare interoperability, or provider-facing tools.

The base salary range for this role is 155,000-185,000 per year. You will also be entitled to receive equity and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on qualifications, experience, and skillset.

Maven embraces a flexible hybrid work model. This role is open to candidates in remote locations with a strong preference for San Francisco, CA; secondary locations include Seattle, WA and New York, NY.

Our teams primarily operate from the New York Metropolitan area, NY, San Francisco/Bay Area, CA, and Seattle, WA. For those in our New York City office, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to work onsite three days a week  (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). For those based in San Francisco/Bay Area, CA, and Seattle, WA, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to attend quarterly Work Together Days within these cities. This policy aims to balance remote work flexibility with the benefits of face-to-face interaction.

title: Ph.D. Position in Computer Science (Wearable Intelligence & Data Fusion)
description:
Constructor University in collaboration with Constructor Knowledge Labs and Constructor Technology

About the Position

The research group of Dr. Sari Sadiya at Constructor Knowledge Labs (CKL), in collaboration with Constructor University (CU) and Constructor Technology (CT), invites applicants for Ph.D. student positions in Computer Science with a focus on wearable intelligence, multimodal data fusion, and edge AI.

The project investigates how wearable data streams can be transformed into structured knowledge and integrated into a knowledge-grounded digital avatar that supports bi-directional collaboration in education and research.

Ph.D. students will work in a highly interdisciplinary environment, combining AI/ML, edge computing, cognitive science, and human–computer interaction. In close collaboration with academia and industry, they will contribute to building privacy-preserving, real-time personalization frameworks while pursuing their doctoral dissertation.

About the Program

The PhD program is research-centered, emphasizing original contributions in:

  • Wearable data analytics and fusion methods
  • Biomedical data analytics
  • On-device processing and performance modeling
  • Personalization and adaptive reasoning systems
  • AI for Education

Doctoral students will also have access to specialized courses in:

  • Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Edge Computing
  • Advanced Computational Methods and Data Science
  • Cognitive Science and Human-Centered Computing

As part of the program, students will collaborate with Constructor Technology to gain first-hand industrial experience, contributing to real-world testbeds and prototypes.

Research Focus

This PhD position is part of the Wearable Intelligence Project, with two main research directions:

  • Data fusion of heterogeneous temporal streams
    • Designing algorithms to unify multimodal signals (physiological, cognitive, contextual, scheduling, and learning data).
    • Developing pipelines that produce structured insights powering the Agentic Personalization Engine (APE).
  • On-device data processing & performance modeling
    • Developing models balancing computation, energy, and data flows across wearable, edge, and cloud environments.
    • Exploring feasibility of running compact micro-LLMs directly on wearables.

The overarching goal is to create scalable, ethical, and transparent personalization systems that support education and research.

Funding

The appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:

  • Monthly stipend of €1,650
  • Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)
  • Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month
  • Supplementary €603 mini-job allowance to support parallel part-time employment (optional)

Constructor Knowledge Labs actively supports candidates in preparing applications for external funding — doctoral scholarships, foundations, or international mobility grants — and can provide institutional support and references

Applicant Profile

Mandatory requirements:

  • MSc degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, AI/ML, Data Science, Cognitive Science, or related disciplines.
  • Strong background in AI/ML, signal processing, or edge computing.
  • Hands-on experience with wearable or multimodal data (e.g., heart rate, EEG, activity, sleep, GPS).
  • Solid mathematical and computational modeling skills.
  • Proficiency in academic English writing (e.g., reports, papers, theses).

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with LLMs, multimodal data fusion, or agent-based AI systems.
  • Familiarity with privacy-preserving ML, dynamic consent, and GDPR-compliant frameworks.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research and collaborate across disciplines.
  • Interest in teaching, mentoring, and applied industrial research.

Application Details

  • Deadline: August 31, 2026

Required documents:

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV);
  • Academic transcripts;
  • Letter of motivation outlining research interests and career goals;
  • 2 recommendation letters.

Applications to be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews.

title: Clinical Data Operator - Austin, TX
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:  On site position in Austin, TX

Clinical Data Operator accessions patient samples according to standard operating procedures (SOP) with high efficiency and accuracy.  Hourly rate starts at $18.
 
Shift Options:
Tuesday - Saturday,  7am-330pm or 9am-5pm
Hourly rate starts at $18
     
 
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

*Front-end lab operations*
- Receive, sort, and transport packages from the shipping dock and reception to the Accessioning lab, and scan tracking numbers accurately.
- Open, prep, and de-kit samples, checking that paperwork matches samples and that no PHI or samples remain in discarded kit boxes.
- Rack bulk samples and distribute work to stations according to distribution guidelines.
- Support sample pickup, consolidation, and send-outs.
- Scan requisitions, bench worksheets, and supporting documents, and upload them to the correct case.
- File, store, and dispose of requisition forms according to retention requirements.
- Empty bins, carts, trash, and biohazard containers, and keep workstations and lab areas clean and organized.

*Case creation and data entry*
- Capture requisition and case information using intelligent document processing (IDP) tools such as Fusion.
- As trained: create new orders in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), enter and review patient data, and keep records accurate and up to date.
- As trained: accession samples across product types with high accuracy and efficiency.

*Quality, safety, and compliance*
- Handle samples (blood, buccal, and tissue) and package-opening tools safely and correctly.
- Escalate packaging issues, discrepancies, or quality concerns to Leads or Supervisors.
- Follow SOPs, quality standards, and safety requirements, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
- This role works with PHI regularly in both paper and electronic form, and has access to various technologies to access PHI in order to do the job. Protect PHI at all times in line with HIPAA and privacy policies.
- Complete HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance, and security training as soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after hire.
- Maintain current status on all Natera training requirements.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT**
- Stand and walk for most of the shift, up to 8–10 hours.
- Lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 lbs regularly, including boxes, totes, and loaded carts.
- Bend, reach, stoop, and kneel repeatedly.
- Perform repetitive hand and wrist motions, including scanning, opening packages, and typing.
- Work in a clinical lab environment with possible exposure to biological samples and biohazardous materials, using required PPE.
- Work in a fast-paced, high-volume, deadline-driven environment.
- Be flexible for shift changes, weekends, holidays, and overtime based on business needs.

**QUALIFICATIONS**
- High school diploma (or equivalent) required.
- 0–1 year of experience in a lab, warehouse, logistics, healthcare, or data entry setting preferred.
- Previous computer experience required.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in high-volume, physical work.
- Willingness to do hands-on tasks of every kind as part of a team.
- Ability to learn several workflows and systems, and build toward full accessioning.
- Typing speed of at least 45 wpm with high accuracy, or the ability to reach it during training.
- Good oral and written communication skills, and sound judgment.
- Reliable, organized, self-motivated, and able to work well with others.

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

For more information, visit www.natera.com.

Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide.

title: AI Solutions Program Manager, Finance
description:
Who we are  

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

You'll be joining the Finance Operational Excellence team, reporting to the Head of Finance Operational Excellence. We are finance transformation and AI experts working side-by-side with Finance, Product, and Engineering teams to redefine processes and build the finance organization of the future. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys working across disciplines: part solution developer, part data architect, part workflow designer, and part coach. You’ll have room to shape how applied AI is built and scaled both from a technical and end-user perspective.

What you’ll do

You'll work side-by-side with Finance subject matter experts to understand how work gets done, identify the highest impact opportunities, and partner with domain teams to chart a transformation plan which balances future ambitions with rapid impact.  You'll work independently to automate manual processes, design and build agents and required data solutions using internal platforms, and enable Finance teams to maintain these solutions long-term. 

You’ll build with your partner teams, not simply deliver solutions to them. You’ll help colleagues move from a manual workflow, to a first AI-enabled win, to a reliable solution they can confidently operate and improve themselves. Success means the workflow stays transformed after the initial build, the team trusts the output, and the people closest to the process can own what comes next. 

You’ll favor learning through building. When possible, you’ll put a useful prototype in front of a Finance user, test it against a real deliverable, and improve it quickly rather than spend weeks describing a theoretical future state. When you encounter platform limitations—which you will—you’ll find creative, supportable approaches, collaborate with Engineering to scope and test custom tools, and escalate strategically when needed.

This role requires a blend of process automation, data operations, technical problem-solving, and stakeholder enablement. You'll spend your time building agents, optimizing data pipelines that feed them, creating knowledge layers that make them more accurate, and training Finance teams to use and maintain them. Success means Finance teams can independently run agents you've built while you provide light support and focus on the next automation opportunity.

Responsibilities

  • Embed with Finance teams to diagnose workflows, identify high-leverage opportunities, and translate business, data, and control requirements into practical AI and automation solutions.
  • Build and operationalize AI agents for Finance use cases, delivering end-to-end solutions from prototype through validation, monitoring, documentation, and handoff.
  • Write and optimize SQL for data extraction, transformation, calculation, and validation, ensuring Finance-facing outputs are accurate, explainable, and reliable.
  • Design reusable knowledge layers, evaluation methods, validation patterns, data-quality frameworks, and components that improve agent accuracy and accelerate future use cases.
  • Identify agentic limitations and new possibilities; determine when to use existing capabilities, develop an alternative approach, or partner with Engineering to scope and test custom tools and integrations, including tools using Model Context Protocol where appropriate.
  • Build alongside users, gather feedback through real deliverables, and iterate until the solution fits the workflow and earns user trust.
  • Enable long-term ownership through clear SOPs, runbooks, training, and self-service tooling; coach Finance teams to operate, maintain, and evolve what has been built.
  • Establish monitoring and observability for deployed agents, including metrics, alerting, and incident-response processes that support reliable operation.
  • Diagnose technical and data issues, resolve problems independently where possible, and collaborate with Engineering when solutions require deeper platform changes.
  • Measure adoption and impact, share lessons and wins, and turn successful implementations into standards, components, and playbooks for the broader Finance AI portfolio.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in data analytics, technical operations, business intelligence, automation, solutions delivery, or a related field.
  • Of which, 2+ years of experience in program management, working directly alongside business leaders to develop and execute process transformation programs
  • Hands-on experience building AI-enabled tools, agents, automations, or workflows that changed a real business process—not solely using AI as a conversational tool, 
  • Strong SQL proficiency, including experience writing complex queries using CTEs, window functions, and joins for data analysis, transformation, or pipeline logic.
  • A track record of independently scoping and delivering technical solutions for process improvement, demonstrating ownership from problem definition through adoption.
  • Strong analytical and investigative skills, including the ability to identify root causes, debug complex data problems, and resolve inconsistencies.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and work effectively with domain experts and Engineering partners.
  • Experience teaching, coaching, enabling users, or transferring ownership of a solution through documentation, training, or self-service tools.
  • Working knowledge of development practices such as version control, testing, code review, and iterative delivery.
  • Experience using low-code tools, scripting, workflow automation, AI-assisted development, or custom integrations, paired with curiosity and the ability to learn evolving technologies.

You will also likely have (not required):

  • Domain experience in Finance Operations, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Payments, or other areas.
  • Familiarity with modern data tools and practices, such as Python, Databricks, ETL/ELT processes, data pipelines, and data-quality controls.

title: Operating Partner (AI Research), London
description:
Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.

The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery. 

Come and be part of an interdisciplinary team driving groundbreaking innovation and play a meaningful role in contributing towards us achieving our ambitious goals, while being a part of an inspiring and collaborative culture.

The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you. 

 

About Iso

Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.

Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.

We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.

Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.

 

Your impact 

As an Operating Partner you'll work as a member of a compact, agile, and high-impact team specialising in catalysing business critical initiatives across Iso through partnership with cross-functional organisational leaders. Together, we drive operational excellence, maximising productivity and accelerating progress toward our mission. Because agility, organisation, and flawless execution are critical, this role will dynamically evolve alongside the needs of our team and the leaders you partner with.

What you will do 

You’ll work alongside the VPs of AI and their wider organisation to deliver the highest-priority initiatives in their org areas, in particular where these are strategic in nature, require cross-organisational influence or are outside of the normal rhythms of the business.

  • Thought-Partner: You’ll enable leaders and their teams to operate effectively by advising and soundboarding on their ideas for how to solve problems, accelerate, and maximise outputs across their organisation 
  • Prioritise and Coordinate: You will distinguish critical leadership priorities from support tasks, establishing clear ownership and empowering teams to act. With a keen sense of timing, you will know when to revive paused initiatives, align stakeholders, and deliver actionable plans.
  • Deliver and Execute: You’ll focus your time on maximising the impact of key initiatives, particularly those outside the normal day-to-day operating patterns, or of the highest strategic importance. You’ll prepare, present and gain agreement on proposals among stakeholders and then influence teams to execute - leveraging strong communication skills. You’ll follow up, problem-solve, close loops in a timely fashion and drive initiatives to completion. 
  • Drive Cross-Functional Collaboration: You’ll build relationships with key stakeholders across Iso to gain a holistic understanding of the organisation, instilling high levels of trust and providing hands-on partnership on important projects.
  • Translate and Communicate: You’ll translate complex technical developments into clear, high-impact executive summaries and strategic presentations for a variety of stakeholders, including board meetings and key management presentations. 
  • Drive efficiency: You’ll empower others to be maximally efficient by optimising for leanness and proactively spotting and breaking down blockers and inefficiencies, balancing what the organisation needs in the short and longer term with a keen eye for how to scale most efficiently and effectively. 

 

Skills and qualifications 

Essential:

  • Executive Partnership & Thought Leadership: Proven track record of operating shoulder-to-shoulder with senior executive leaders (e.g., C-Suite, VP-level) as a trusted advisor, strategic soundboard, and operational force-multiplier.
  • Understand and Translate Complex Topics with Fluency: Strong ability to learn and absorb technical information, grasp key concepts of machine learning/frontier AI, with the confidence to probe, synthesize, and translate complex technical matters into actionable executive communication.
  • Complex Execution & Ambiguity: Demonstrated ability to break down highly ambiguous, multi-faceted problems into concrete plans and drive them through to measurable completion with pace and precision.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Proven ability to build rapid trust and drive alignment across diverse, interdisciplinary teams (research, engineering, product, and operations) without direct line authority.
  • Agility & Low-Ego Mindset: High resilience and adaptability in dynamic scale-up environments, with a roll-up-your-sleeves mentality where no task is too big or too small.

Nice to have:

  • Background in a Chief of Staff, Strategic Operations, or Operating Partner role within a fast-scaling tech or AI organization.
  • Familiarity or working exposure to digital biology, computational chemistry, or biopharma workflows.
  • Experience facilitating executive team rhythms, planning cycles, and organizational scaling mechanisms.


Culture and values

We are guided by our shared values. It's not about finding people who think and act in the same way. These values help to guide our work and will continue to strengthen it. 

Thoughtful
Thoughtful at Iso is about curiosity, creativity and care. It is about good people doing good, rigorous and future-making science every single day.

Brave
Brave at Iso is about fearlessness, but it’s also about initiative and integrity. The scale of the challenge demands nothing less.

Determined
Determined at Iso is the way we pursue our goal. It’s a confidence in our hypothesis, as well as the urgency and agility needed to deliver on it. Because disease won’t wait, so neither should we.

Together
Together at Iso is about connection, collaboration across fields and catalytic relationships. It’s knowing that transformation is a group project, and remembering that what we’re doing will have a real impact on real people everywhere.


Creating an extraordinary company

We believe that to be successful we need a team with a range of skills and talents. We're building an environment where collaboration is fundamental, learning is shared and every employee feels supported and able to thrive. We value unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, and perspectives, and harness these qualities to create extraordinary impact.

We are committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis protected by applicable law. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.


Hybrid working

It’s hugely important for us to share knowledge and build strong relationships with each other, and we find it easier to do this if we spend time together in person. This is why we follow a hybrid model, and would require you to be able to come into the office 3 days a week (currently Tuesday, Wednesday, and one other day depending on which team you’re in). If you have additional needs that would prevent you from following this hybrid approach, we’d be happy to talk through these if you’re selected for an initial screening call.

We're looking for someone with an engineering-minded, "application scientist" type approach — comfortable understanding the technical requirements involved in onboarding a partner, and operating confidently within a large company mindset and environment.

In this role you will get to:

  • Define, build, and execute the technical partner strategy, prioritising which integrations and joint solutions to build, developing and implementing joint go-to-market plans (co-sell, co-build, co-deliver), aligning teams and facilitating sales enablement and training of partners.

  • Scope integration feasibility early in partner conversations, translating vague partner asks into clear, buildable technical specifications and setting realistic expectations.

  • Engage partners to develop differentiated solutions through joint collaboration, market and competitive analysis, and the creation of joint marketing collateral.
  • Evangelise partnerships internally, working closely with Sales, Legal, Marketing, Engineering, Product, Support and Pre-Sales stakeholders, and with colleagues at Siemens, feeding partner needs into the roadmap and organising collaborative events.
  • Define, track and analyse key partnership metrics, collaborating with partners to optimise performance, and represent Dotmatics/Siemens at alliance and partner conferences and events.
  • Focus specifically on systems integration partners, bringing on partners that will meaningfully increase the bottom line.

We are looking for candidate's who have 7+ years in technology partnerships, alliances, solution architecture or pre-sales engineering, including several years leading strategic technical partner or ISV relationships at enterprise scale. You've built integrations, not just managed them, and you can move fluently between a business review and a whiteboard session with a partner's engineers. You're comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy on complex, ambiguous pursuits, and you set realistic expectations that engineering can actually deliver on.

Just as importantly, you lead through influence. You can align engineering, marketing and sales teams, internally and across partner organisations, behind a shared plan without direct authority, and you're motivated by building a partnering function and team, not just running one. While not a traditional "sales" person, you're comfortable navigating sales-style conversations, combining technical knowledge with strong relationship management and communication skills.

  • Technical partnership leadership - a proven track record defining and executing partner or alliance strategy with ISVs, technology platforms or system integrators, with measurable partner-sourced or partner-influenced revenue impact.
